title: Security review: EU-US data sovereignty + subprocessor mapping — Bluepine Energy
next_steps: Send full subprocessor inventory and SOC2 report link
Schedule 1:1 technical region-pinning test with Bluepine infra team (Diego + Arjun)
Share draft contract language for EU-only processing appendix
action_items: Diego Ramos - run region pinning test on sample payloads using Bluepine test tenant - due 2026-02-21
Maya Patel - send SOC 2 + ISO summary doc and subprocessor spreadsheet - due 2026-02-16
Ella Chen - provide authorized contact list for KMS onboarding - due 2026-02-19
summary: Customer is evaluating Redwood for inference serving for EU operations; main concerns are strict EU-only processing, cross-border fallback policies, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and an up-to-date subprocessor list. Redwood AE/SE walked through region pinning architecture, fallback model variants, and contract controls. Agreed to run a test to validate region affinity and to share SOC2/ISO evidence and subprocessor inventory.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today, we have about 50 minutes on the calendar. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Sofia (Bluepine): Sofia Lindqvist here, CISO at Bluepine.
[00:10] Markus (Bluepine): Markus Vogel, head of cloud engineering.
[00:12] Ella (Bluepine): Ella Chen, legal ops.
[00:14] Arjun (Bluepine): Arjun Patel, platform eng.
[00:17] Maya (Redwood): And from our side Diego Ramos, solutions engineer, and Priya Nair from security program. Diego will cover the technical flow and Priya will clarify compliance bits.
[00:26] Diego (Redwood SE): hi all, excited to dig in. Quick agenda: region pinning mechanics, how we enforce EU-only processing, KMS/customer-managed key flow, and subprocessor map.
[00:35] Sofia: Great, our board is expecting a firm answer on EU-only processing and proof that no EU data crosses the Atlantic for inference. We also need to understand what happens if capacity in eu-west is exhausted — is there cross-border fallback?
[00:48] Maya: totally, we'll be explicit about that. To start: Redwood supports region affinity — requests can be routed to eu-west-1 handlers only when configured, and we can disable cross-border fallback in the customer config. Diego will show the architecture.
[01:02] Diego: right. At a high level we have a control plane and a data plane — the control plane is global but metadata-only, it never persists payloads. The data plane is regional. When you pin to EU-only, all inference requests and KV caches stay within the eu region. We can also provide a private deployment (VPC) so compute and storage are in your project VPC.
[01:22] Markus: when you say the control plane is global, does that mean any metadata or call traces go outside EU? We have to avoid even metadata leakage for certain datasets.
[01:30] Priya (Redwood): good point. For customers that require minimal metadata egress we offer an option to run a private control plane in-region — that's our Private offering. For hosted customers we also pseudonymize and limit telemetry; full audit logs can be stored in-region if you use our log-forwarding to your SIEM.
[01:48] Sofia: Can you send a diagram?
[01:50] Maya: yes, we'll send the architecture diagram and a short whiteboard. Link noted: we'll attach in the follow-up.
[01:57] Diego: Also worth noting fallback policies: default behavior allows falling back to nearest compatible model in another region for availability. But you can configure a strict policy 'eu-only' which returns a 503 when capacity is exceeded rather than cross-border failover. That is recorded on the per-tenant config.
[02:14] Ella: From legal: we need contractual language that says Bluepine can require EU-only processing and that Redwood maintains an up-to-date list of subprocessors located outside the EU. Do you have a subprocessors manifest?
[02:25] Priya: yes, we maintain a subprocessor registry — we can provide the current snapshot and a regular cadence for updates. That includes cloud infra partners, telemetry storage, and model hosting partners. We'll share a CSV.
[02:36] Sofia: Are any of your subprocessors US-based and involved in data plane? That's the big concern.
[02:42] Diego: Most critical data plane components for EU-only customers run on regional cloud tenants (eu-* zones). Our infra providers may be global — for example underlying cloud compute might have US corporate control — but we can guarantee the processing locality and contractual commitments. We also support contract addenda for EU-only processing.
[02:58] Markus: ok. I need to understand KMS flow — we want customer-managed keys and not have Redwood hold plaintext. How does that look?
[03:05] Diego: we integrate with customer KMS via standard envelope encryption. You provide the CMK and we perform encryption/decryption locally in the region. Redwood can store only the ciphertext; we do not have the raw key material. We also support HSM-backed keys.
[03:20] Arjun: so you'll call our KMS for every new session or per-inference? Latency is a concern.
[03:25] Diego: we use a short-lived data key cache: the data key is retrieved and cached in the regional runtime for a bounded TTL, so you don't call KMS on every token. We can tune TTL vs security. Typical pattern is 1–15 minutes depending on your policy.
[03:39] Sofia: do you have a diagram or sequence for the KMS handshake?
[03:43] Diego: yes, we'll attach the sequence diagram. It shows CMK in your KMS -> Redwood runtime requests wrapped key -> decrypts locally using the wrapped key. All requests to KMS are from within the customer-controlled network if you choose VPC private deployment.
[03:57] Ella: We need proof points — SOC2 type II, ISO27001 coverage, and recent penetration test summary.
[04:04] Priya: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, ISO27001 certificate snapshot, and a red-team summary redacted for IP. We'll bundle those in the follow up.
[04:13] Sofia: audit logs are also critical — we need immutable logs for all admin actions and API calls with user identity mapping to our SSO.
[04:21] Diego: audit trail is available; we keep admin audit logs and can forward them to your log retention. For SSO we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, SCIM provisioning for user sync, and RBAC roles.
[04:34] Markus: if we onboard via Dedicated or Private, can we manage RBAC entirely ourselves? We want to tie roles to our AD groups.
[04:40] Priya: yes — with Private we support full delegated auth and you can sync groups through SCIM. With Dedicated we can map RBAC to your SSO; we still have an admin plane but you control most role assignments.
[04:50] Sofia: are audit logs tamper-evident? We prefer append-only with hash chaining or forward to our syslog collector.
[04:57] Diego: we support both: append-only in our internal store with write-once semantics and you can push logs to your SIEM over TLS; the SIEM will be the source-of-truth. For high-assurance customers we can set up signed log exports.
[05:10] Ella: about subprocessor notification: how much advance notice do you provide when onboarding a new subprocessor? Contractually we want 30 days notice and an opt-out for high-risk subprocessors.
[05:20] Priya: our standard is 30 days for material subprocessors; we can agree to a contract clause for an opt-out for specific categories. We'll bring legal on the next call if needed.
[05:29] Sofia: good. One more on data residency — how do you prove to auditors that a given inference for a user in EU did not leave the EU? Is there a traceable artifact?
[05:38] Diego: yes: we can emit request-level metadata showing region handled, host identifiers, and signed timestamps. Those artifacts can be exported to your log store and used as evidence in audits. They do not include payload content unless you request that.
[05:52] Markus: what about model weights? If you host a model variant in US but the EU uses a different replica, what prevents accidental weight sync?
[05:59] Diego: model artifacts are region-scoped; when you choose EU-only we pin model replicas to eu buckets. Cross-region replication is disabled for that tenant. There is an admin toggle that requires two-person approval for any replication change.
[06:12] Sofia: latency vs capacity again — we cannot accept silent throttling with cross-border fallback without board approval. We'll prefer immediate 503 on capacity issues. Is that possible?
[06:22] Maya: yes, that's the strict policy I referenced earlier. We'll put that in the tenant config and reflect in the contract.
[06:28] Arjun: from the engineering side, we'd like to run a region-pinning smoke test with sample workloads and look at request traces. Diego can we do that in a sandbox?
[06:36] Diego: absolutely — we'll provision a test tenant in eu-west and generate synthetic traffic, share traces and signed metadata. We can also re-run with KMS enabled.
[06:45] Ella: about subprocessors — we saw mention of a telemetry partner that stores logs. Are they located in the US?
[06:51] Priya: our telemetry partner does have US-operated regions, but for EU customers we can configure telemetry to use EU storage endpoints only. We'll map the specific partners and endpoints in the spreadsheet.
[07:02] Sofia: ok, so next steps: send us SOC2 and subprocessor CSV, run test tenant, and share KMS sequence diagram. Anything else?
[07:09] Maya: we'll also draft proposed contract language for EU-only appendix and notice period for subprocessors.
[07:14] Markus: timeline wise we need validation in two weeks to present to procurement. Can you meet that?
[07:19] Maya: yes, Diego — can you run the tests and Priya will assemble the compliance pack.
[07:24] Diego: will do. I'll schedule the test and share results by 2026-02-21.
[07:29] Priya: I'll share SOC2 artifacts under NDA by EOD Monday.
[07:33] Ella: legal will review the proposed contractual language; I'll send markups after I see the draft.
[07:37] Sofia: couple quick technical clarifications: how do you handle caching for prefix completions — does any cached KV leak outside region?
[07:46] Diego: KV caches are regional and tenant-scoped. For EU-only tenants caches live in-region and are purged on tenant delete. We don't shard KV to other regions.
[07:56] Arjun: nice. Also, for longer-running sessions do you rotate session keys? You mentioned TTL — can TTL be under one minute for high-security contexts?
[08:04] Diego: yes, TTL is configurable, down to 30 seconds, but that adds KMS call frequency. We'll show perf impact in the test.
[08:12] Maya: small note on documentation: we have a public security page but we'll share the NDA package for sensitive artifacts. Link: [redwood-security-docs] (we'll attach).
[08:21] Sofia: can you briefly describe what 'private control plane' entails?
[08:25] Priya: private control plane means we deploy our orchestration components into a customer-managed VPC or a dedicated project where you control network egress and the control APIs are reachable only from permitted IPs. It eliminates the need for global control-plane telemetry to leave region.
[08:40] Markus: what's the onboarding lift? If we go Private, are we managing upgrades?
[08:44] Diego: we handle upgrades but we coordinate maintenance windows. For Private we offer runbook access and can provide a managed ops support add-on.
[08:52] Sofia: regarding certifications — is your SOC2 scope covering the Private deployment as well or do we need separate evidence?
[08:58] Priya: SOC2 covers our service baseline; for Private deployments we provide a deployment-specific attestation and can include the deployment in our SOC scope for larger contracts. We'll include language in the compliance pack.
[09:10] Ella: question on data deletion: if we request deletion for a tenant, what is the timeline and is that certificate provided?
[09:17] Diego: standard deletion is 30 days for backups and 7 days for live storage; we can expedite to 7 days total for EU-only tenants on contract, with a deletion certificate provided. We'll spell that out in the SLA addendum.
[09:29] Sofia: good. Can you give an example of the signed metadata artifact format? We want something we can slot into audit reports.
[09:36] Diego: it's a JSON blob with fields for request_id, tenant_id, region, host_id, timestamp, and a signature header. Example in the follow-up. The signature is HSM-backed and verifiable.
[09:46] Markus: one more — model evals and snapshots; if we run A/B tests, do those logs contain user content? We need to ensure that any evaluation harness strips PII before storing.
[09:55] Priya: evaluation logs can be configured to omit payloads; we support redaction at ingestion and on-demand ephemeral evaluation modes where we never persist user content. We'll document the options.
[10:06] Maya: sounds like we're aligned on next steps. Anything else from Bluepine?
[10:10] Sofia: not from me; I appreciate the clarity.
[10:13] Ella: no.
[10:14] Arjun: no.
[10:15] Maya: ok we'll follow up with the pack and the sandbox invite. Thanks everyone.
[10:20] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional hesitations and overlap; some product proper nouns may have small mis-transcriptions like 'KV' sometimes typed as 'K V' in the auto transcript. Shared artifacts: security pack link (to be sent under NDA), region-pinning whiteboard, and subprocessor CSV.
